# Output Format Reference

Templates for all files generated by project-onboard.
Read this file BEFORE generating any output.

## AGENTS.md Template

AGENTS.md is the preferred canonical instruction file. It is a decision tree
for the AI agent, NOT documentation for humans. Keep it under 150 lines. Use
task-based routing.

```markdown
<!-- generated by project-onboard -->
# Project: {name}
{one-liner description from README or interview}

## Tech Stack
{auto-detected: framework, language, ORM, DB, etc.}

## Commands
- Dev: `{dev command}`
- Build: `{build command}`
- Test: `{test command}`
- Lint: `{lint command}`
{add more from package.json scripts or Makefile as relevant}

## ⚡ Context Available — DO NOT explore
Context files are pre-generated in .context/.
Read ONLY the files relevant to your current task.
DO NOT run find/ls/tree to explore. Trust these files.
Last updated: {date} | Run /onboard-update to refresh

## When to read what

BEFORE modifying or creating any page, screen, or route:
  → read .context/features/pages-routing.md
  → read .context/features/_feature-map.md

BEFORE modifying app state (stores/slices/providers):
  → read .context/features/state-data.md
  → read .context/features/pages-routing.md (check consumers)

BEFORE modifying UI components, theming, forms, or i18n:
  → read .context/features/design-system.md

BEFORE modifying or creating any API endpoint or middleware:
  → read .context/features/api-middleware.md
  → read .context/features/pages-routing.md (check callers)

BEFORE modifying database schema, caching, or migrations:
  → read .context/features/data-layer.md
  → read .context/features/_feature-map.md (check impact)

BEFORE modifying auth, permissions, or security config:
  → read .context/features/auth-security.md

BEFORE modifying background jobs, events, or service communication:
  → read .context/features/background-events.md

BEFORE modifying external integrations, logging, or config:
  → read .context/features/integrations-infra.md

BEFORE writing or modifying tests:
  → read .context/testing-strategy.md

WHEN you need to understand how a feature works end-to-end:
  → read .context/features/_feature-map.md

WHEN you need to understand project architecture or patterns:
  → read .context/architecture.md
  → read .context/conventions.md

WHEN you encounter domain terms you don't understand:
  → read .context/business.md

WHEN deploying or working with CI/CD:
  → read .context/workflow.md

WHEN using a framework API you're unsure about:
  → read .context/stack-docs/

## Warnings
{top 3-5 critical warnings inline}
- Full list: read .context/warnings.md

## Testing
{one-line strategy summary, e.g., "TDD, Vitest, target 80%"}
- Details: read .context/testing-strategy.md
<!-- end generated by project-onboard -->
```

## CLAUDE.md Shim Templates

Use CLAUDE.md as a compatibility shim unless the user explicitly chooses to
keep an existing CLAUDE.md as canonical.

### CLAUDE.md points to AGENTS.md

Use this when AGENTS.md is canonical:

```markdown
<!-- generated by project-onboard -->
# Claude Code Instructions

The canonical agent instructions for this project live in `AGENTS.md`.

Read `AGENTS.md` before making changes. It routes you to the relevant
`.context/` files for architecture, conventions, workflow, warnings, and
feature maps.
<!-- end generated by project-onboard -->
```

### AGENTS.md points to CLAUDE.md

Use this only when the user chooses to keep an existing CLAUDE.md as canonical:

```markdown
<!-- generated by project-onboard -->
# Agent Instructions

The canonical instructions for this project currently live in `CLAUDE.md`.

Read `CLAUDE.md` before making changes. It routes you to the relevant
`.context/` files for architecture, conventions, workflow, warnings, and
feature maps.
<!-- end generated by project-onboard -->
```

## Instruction File Selection Rules

Use `AGENTS.md` (plural) as the default canonical file. Do not create
`AGENT.md` singular.

1. If neither `AGENTS.md` nor `CLAUDE.md` exists:
   - Write the full task-routed template to `AGENTS.md`
   - Write a CLAUDE.md shim pointing to `AGENTS.md`
2. If `AGENTS.md` exists and `CLAUDE.md` does not:
   - Preserve and merge generated sections into `AGENTS.md`
   - Write a CLAUDE.md shim pointing to `AGENTS.md`
3. If `CLAUDE.md` exists and `AGENTS.md` does not:
   - Ask whether to migrate content into `AGENTS.md` or keep `CLAUDE.md`
     canonical
   - If migrating, preserve CLAUDE.md content inside `AGENTS.md`, then replace
     `CLAUDE.md` with a shim pointing to `AGENTS.md`
   - If keeping Claude canonical, preserve and merge into `CLAUDE.md`, then
     write `AGENTS.md` as a shim pointing to `CLAUDE.md`
4. If both files exist:
   - Read both
   - Prefer `AGENTS.md` as canonical unless `CLAUDE.md` clearly has newer or
     more complete user-written instructions
   - Ask before merging if the canonical choice is ambiguous
   - Keep the non-canonical file as a shim

Never discard user-written instruction content. Replace an existing file with a
shim only after its original content is migrated into the canonical file or the
user explicitly chooses that direction.

### Rules for Canonical Instruction Files

1. NEVER exceed 150 lines
2. NEVER just list files — always use BEFORE/WHEN routing
3. NEVER include information that belongs in context files
4. ALWAYS preserve existing user-written content when merging
5. Mark generated sections with HTML comments
6. Include the "DO NOT explore" instruction — this is critical

## Context File Templates

Every context file follows this structure:

```markdown
# {Title}
> Read this file WHEN {trigger condition}.

## How to use
{1-2 lines explaining what the agent should do with this info}

## Content
{structured, concise, actionable content}
```

### architecture.md

```markdown
# Architecture
> Read this file WHEN you need to understand project structure or patterns.

## How to use
Use this as your map. Do NOT run find/ls/tree — this file is your source of truth.

## Directory Structure
{tree output of key directories, 2 levels deep, annotated}

src/
  app/           → Next.js App Router pages + API routes ({N} routes)
  components/    → Shared React components ({N} files)
  lib/           → Utilities, DB client, helpers
  services/      → Business logic layer
  types/         → TypeScript type definitions
prisma/          → Database schema + migrations

## Key Architecture Decisions
- {pattern}: {why and how}
- {pattern}: {why and how}

## Key Files
- {path} → {what it does, when you'd need to read it}
```

### conventions.md

```markdown
# Conventions
> Read this file WHEN writing new code or reviewing patterns.

## How to use
Follow these conventions for all new code. Check existing code matches.

## Code Style
{from eslint/biome/prettier config}

## Naming
- Files: {pattern, e.g., kebab-case.ts}
- Components: {pattern, e.g., PascalCase}
- Functions: {pattern}
- Database: {pattern}

## Patterns
- {pattern name}: {brief description}
  Example: {one-line code example}

## Import Order
{if detectable from config or existing code}
```

### workflow.md

```markdown
# Workflow
> Read this file WHEN deploying, working with CI/CD, or branching.

## How to use
Follow this process for all code changes.

## Branch Strategy
{detected from git branches or interview}

## CI/CD Pipeline
{from GitHub Actions / GitLab CI config}
- Trigger: {when}
- Steps: {what runs}

## Deploy
- Target: {Vercel/AWS/Docker/etc.}
- Command: {how}
- Environments: {staging, production, etc.}

## Git Hooks
{from .husky/ or pre-commit config}
```

### business.md

```markdown
# Business Context
> Read this file WHEN you encounter domain terms or need project context.

## How to use
Reference these terms when reading or writing code that uses domain language.

## What This Project Does
{from README + interview}

## Domain Terms
| Term | Meaning |
|------|---------|
| {term} | {definition} |

## Users
{who uses this and how}
```

### testing-strategy.md

```markdown
# Testing Strategy
> Read this file BEFORE writing or modifying any tests.

## How to use
Follow this strategy for all test-related work.

## Approach
{TDD / test-after / none — from interview}

## Frameworks
- Unit/Integration: {vitest/jest/etc.}
- E2E: {playwright/cypress/none}

## Coverage
- Target: {X%}
- Current: ~{Y%} ({N} test files found)

## What to Test
- Unit: {what}
- Integration: {what}
- E2E: {what}

## Rules
{from interview, e.g., "write test before code", "every PR needs tests"}
```

### warnings.md

```markdown
# Warnings
> Read this file WHEN planning any significant change.

## How to use
Check this list before modifying files. Ask the user if unsure.

## Do Not Modify Without Asking
- {path}: {reason}

## Common Pitfalls
- {pitfall}: {how to avoid}

## Breaking Change Risk
- {area}: {why it's risky}
```
